learning_outcomes.text: Students develop a basic understanding of dynamic system analogies.
Students learn the time domain and frequency domain criteria for transient and steady-state system performance.
Students gain knowledge about time domain and frequency domain techniques for stability analysis such as root-locus, Bode, and Nyquist plots.
Students gain experience with controller and compensator design for reference tracking.
Students are introduced to robustness analysis through disturbance rejection methods.

syllabus_topics: Mathematical expression of first and second order linear, time-invariant system dynamics
Time and Frequency Domain response of dynamic systems
Feedback control examples from Neuromuscular, Cardiovascular, and Endocrine Systems
bibliography: Khoo MCK, Physiological Control Systems, IEEE Press Series in BME, 2000
